subject: Business
title: The First Coins: Lydia's Revolution
description: Learn The First Coins: Lydia's Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: Around 600 BCE, King Alyattes of Lydia stamped lumps of electrum with a lion's head. Money got official.

buildup.text: Coins solved a huge problem: standardized weight and purity guaranteed by the king's seal.

discovery.text: Before coins, every metal transaction required weighing and testing. Coins made commerce instant.

twist.text: Kings quickly learned they could mix in cheaper metals. Currency debasement was invented alongside coins.

climax.text: Lydia became fabulously wealthy from trade — so rich that King Croesus is still synonymous with wealth.

punchline.text: The first coin was also the first government-backed promise.

quiz.question: What problem did the first coins solve?
options: Standardized weight and purity guaranteed by authority
The need to carry large amounts of grain

details.summary: The Kingdom of Lydia in modern-day Turkey minted the first standardized coins around 600 BCE from electrum, a natural gold-silver alloy. Standard weight and government stamps eliminated the need to weigh and verify metal in every transaction, revolutionizing commerce.
details.whyItMatters: Standardized coinage was a transformative monetary innovation that enabled efficient trade across vast distances. The concept of government-stamped guaranteed currency established trust mechanisms that underpin modern money systems.
takeaways: Lydia minted the first standardized coins around 600 BCE in modern Turkey
Government stamps guaranteed weight and purity without individual testing
Coinage enabled efficient trade that fueled economic growth across the ancient world

faq.question: What problem did standardized coins solve?
faq.answer: Before coins, each precious metal transaction required weighing and testing purity. This was slow and required expertise. Coins with a government stamp guaranteed a specific weight and purity, allowing instant trust between strangers and dramatically speeding up trade.

faq.question: How did coinage spread from Lydia to the rest of the world?
faq.answer: Greek cities quickly adopted the innovation and refined it with distinct city stamps. Alexander the Great spread standard coinage across his empire. Roman coins built on Greek designs. Chinese, Indian, and other civilizations independently developed similar coinage systems.
